correctness.rationale: Slicing at S=sum X_i gives density n s^(n−1)/(1−t^n) and independent uniform barycentric proportions. Their second-moment matrix yields transverse eigenvalue E[S²]/[n(n+1)] and axial eigenvalue Var(S)/n; dividing their determinant by (a/n!)² proves the stated profile and simplex baseline. For the derivative, an independent formal chain rule in t and u=t^n recovers the sparse numerator −n(n+2)t^(n−1)(1−t)B_n. Analyticity of H at 1 follows by setting S=1−hY: the law of Y on [0,1] has a normalized polynomial weight, and the factor h² in Var(S) cancels the volume-square factor. The substitutions a(1/t)=−t^−n a(t), and likewise for b,c, give H(1/t)=H(t) and H'(1)=0. With the derivative prefactors, this forces (1−t)^6 to divide B_n. Its quotient has degree 2n−3 and is palindromic. Its coefficients through degree n−2 come from ((n−1)−(n+3)t)/(1−t)^6 and equal positive [(5(n−1)−4j)/5] binom(j+4,4); reflection covers every coefficient including n=2. Thus H'<0 on (0,1), with continuity giving strict decrease from t=0 too. Expanding E and a gives the first deficit (n−1)(n+2)t^n. The thin slice has E[S²]→1 and Var(S)/h²→1/12; using volume a/n! gives the stated finite endpoint and e²/12 dimensional limit. Independent second-order expansion using the density of Y proportional to (1−hY)^(n−1) gives zero linear term and relative quadratic term (n−1)(n+3)h²/30. Both coefficients are nonzero for all n≥2; no assertion assigns an isotropic constant to the degenerate t=1 body.
residual_risks: The independent checks concern this single-vertex family only; no use is made of a global simplex extremum claim.

The exact, different contact orders quantify how weakly a small removed cap changes this invariant and how the normalized thin endpoint is reached. The coefficient mechanism is uniform, not an isolated depth sample or a recasting of the known dimension-three calculation.
